title: The interface: HUD, menus, journal and inventory
outputs_written: game/src/ui/glyphs.js — the two faces as quadratic outline data (RI-UIX06 A3/G2, M-F17.3)
game/src/ui/theme.js — the nine materials, palette drawn from corpus/50-world/regions.json (AD4 = ΔE 0)
game/src/ui/surface.js — the second composited quad + the element register (el() is the only way to draw)
game/src/ui/chrome.js — screen/tagColumn/row/letterRing; paper-aware ink; no card/button/tab/modal helper exists
game/src/ui/hud.js — E1..E11, bars as bone troughs
game/src/ui/system.js — modes, focus, the S14 pause rule, navigable[], getUIState payload
game/data/items/carried.json — 44 items, 9 categories, desc mean 28w, item:dialogue ratio 0.023
game/data/states/ui-journal.json — RI-UIX04's mandated fixture: 5 quests, 19 entries, interleave 0.889
game/data/progression/levels.json — REPLACED with RI-PRG01's canonical curve (see findings)
findings: ARCHITECTURE (binding): __HARNESS.screenshot() is canvas.toDataURL(). game/src/render/ui.js draws into an offscreen 2D canvas and composites it as a textured quad. W1-21 follows it exactly: Renderer.menus = new UISurface(w,h), composited after the dialogue surface and before the title surface. NO DOM anywhere in this interface.

Renderer.setSize() resizes the UI canvas to the drawing buffer, so texel:pixel is 1:1 and there is nothing to upscale — that is what makes RI-UIX06 M-F17.2 (DPR-2 stem sharpness) passable from a canvas path. Texture filters are NearestFilter both ways; a LINEAR filter on a 1:1 blit would soften every glyph for nothing.

DESIGN DECISION, contradicts the dispatch brief: THERE IS NO MAP SCREEN. openMenu('map') throws with the reason. The brief said 'the map is Morrowind's and has no quest pins'; RI-UIX04 JU8 says 'map unreachable AND non-existent', calls the existence half the one that matters, and makes a map a hard fail plus AR-2 via Q7. RI-UIX02 §F's own compromise is taken instead: the compass is a boxed ITEM (shore-compass) you stop and open, and the charts are a pilot's PROSE directions (pilots-chart-book) read on the book screen. Both are objects with weight in the inventory. A critic may overrule this; the route is a seam ruling, not a code change.

DATA DEFECT FIXED: game/data/progression/levels.json carried soul_cost_formula 'round(0.02L^3+3.06L^2+105.6L-895)', which is NEGATIVE below level 9, plus a 5-row table whose values (673,689,706,723) are the DARK SOULS reference column of RI-PRG01's table, not ours, plus a 6-name Souls attribute list contradicting attributes.json's ten. The level-up screen showed souls-to-next = 0 at level 6 and RI-UIX03 L3 was unpassable by any build. Replaced with RI-PRG01's canonical formula and its own 139-row table; formula and table agree on all 139 rows.

CONSUMPTION FIXED: burden. burdenTierOf/_burdenMult/traversal.step consumed sim.player.burdenRatio every frame, and the ONLY thing that ever set it was the harness verb setBurden(). Carrying 44 objects cost nothing. Engine._recomputeBurden() now sets it from the same weight sum the inventory screen prints, every step. Perturbation: adding the hauberk + maul moves the tier and _burdenMult() returns 0.90, which sim/traversal.js applies as a speed.

MARKER-SCAN DEPARTURE, declared: RI-UIX02 §B's F2 key regex /(pos|coord|location|xyz|latlon)/i is an unanchored substring and returns 300 hits on the shipped tree, ALL of them the word 'disposition'. Matched as a word instead; self-test asserts target_pos / destination_coord / position / poi_location / xyz still fire and disposition / composition do not.

One declared marker-scan exception: stealth/detection.json:no_meter.hud_elements = 0 (F1's hud_.* branch catching W1-15's DECLARATION that stealth draws no HUD elements). Recorded in tools/analysis/marker-scan-exceptions.json with what removes it; a stale declaration fails the run.

getUIState() rewritten. It BUILDS the layout for the current frame before reporting, because every probe runs setRenderRate(0) and a HUD that only existed during a render would report the frame before last to RI-UIX01 D1 ('100% of frames within ±0.005').
Measured at 1920x1080, ui-journal fixture: HUD 6 persistent elements, union coverage 2.0457% of frame (RI-UIX01 §C budget 4.0%, hard fail 8.0%). Menu panel area_frac 0.5718 (P5 cap 0.60).
Pause rule measured: openMenu('inventory') out of combat, stepFrames(120), getFrame() 0 -> 0. In-combat behaviour still to be measured.

Journal measured: 19 entries declared as elements in chronological order, 12 visible on the spread, interleave_ratio 0.8889 (JU2 bar 0.5, hard fail 0.30; the grouped-view ceiling for a 5-quest/19-entry fixture is 0.222). uiSearch('ledger') returns 1 result, chronological true.

Book layout retuned twice against RI-UIX05 §A: 26 px type, leading 1.46, 46-65 chars/line, full pages 112-172 words. The per-BOOK words/page median is ~102, below B1's 120-180, because half the shipped readables are 100-150 word notes — the library is W1-17's and RI-LOR03's median book is ~520 words. Declared content gap, not a layout defect: the FULL pages are in band.

CONTRAST BUG FOUND AND FIXED by looking at the render: the inventory drew iron-gall ink (L 0.014) on a reed ground (L 0.038) = 1.4:1, unreadable. chrome.js now derives the ink from the ground's luminance and every screen asks for ink()/inkDim(); paperContrast() reports the pair it chose.
next_step: remaining tools: ui-census, ui-layer, marker-diff, ui-forbidden, journal-ui, text-metrics, ui-metrics. Then the in-combat pause/occlusion/input measurements and the harness-vs-page screenshot diff.
notes_for_successor: The one thing that must not regress: UISurface.el() is the ONLY drawing entry point and it clips the callback to the rect it declared, so the census and the pixels cannot disagree. If someone adds a raw ctx accessor, RI-UIX02 K2 stops meaning anything. Screens are pure functions of a model assembled in UISystem._*Model(); the engine's _uiCtx() is the only place that reads the simulation.
